# Dates

Get the current time, move a date by days or hours, and take a date apart.

**Library:** [Standard library](index.md#standard-library), for apps and code-pipeline hooks. More in [Cogniscript](../../../concepts/cogniscript.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`DateAddDays`](#dateadddays) | Adds a number of days to a date and returns the new date. |
| [`DateAddHours`](#dateaddhours) | Adds a number of hours to a date and returns the new date, moving to another day when it needs to. |
| [`DateDiff`](#datediff) | Returns the time between two dates in milliseconds: `left` minus `right`. |
| [`DateGetDay`](#dategetday) | Returns the day of the month of a date, from 1 to 31. |
| [`DateGetMonth`](#dategetmonth) | Returns the month of a date, from 1 (January) to 12 (December). |
| [`DateGetUtc`](#dategetutc) | Returns the current date and time in UTC. |
| [`DateGetYear`](#dategetyear) | Returns the year of a date, such as 2026. |

### DateAddDays

Adds a number of days to a date and returns the new date. The time of day stays the same.

```c
date DateAddDays(date date, int days)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `date` | `date` | The date to start from. Text such as `2026-11-02` works too. |
| `days` | `int` | The number of days to add. Use a negative number to go back. |

**Returns** `date`: The new date.

### DateAddHours

Adds a number of hours to a date and returns the new date, moving to another day when it needs to.

```c
date DateAddHours(date date, int hours)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `date` | `date` | The date to start from. Text such as `2026-11-02 14:30` works too. |
| `hours` | `int` | The number of hours to add. Use a negative number to go back. |

**Returns** `date`: The new date.

### DateDiff

Returns the time between two dates in milliseconds: `left` minus `right`.

```c
decimal DateDiff(date left, date right)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `left` | `date` | The later date, usually. |
| `right` | `date` | The date to subtract from `left`. |

**Returns** `decimal`: The difference in milliseconds.

The result is negative when `left` is the earlier date. Divide it by 1000 for seconds, 60000 for minutes, 3600000 for hours or 86400000 for days. A stored `date` keeps whole seconds, so the difference between two stored dates is a whole number of seconds.

### DateGetDay

Returns the day of the month of a date, from 1 to 31.

```c
int DateGetDay(date date)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `date` | `date` | The date. Text such as `2026-11-02` works too. |

**Returns** `int`: The day of the month.

### DateGetMonth

Returns the month of a date, from 1 (January) to 12 (December).

```c
int DateGetMonth(date date)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `date` | `date` | The date. Text such as `2026-11-02` works too. |

**Returns** `int`: The month.

### DateGetUtc

Returns the current date and time in UTC.

```c
date DateGetUtc()
```

**Returns** `date`: The current UTC date and time.

The value is stored as text such as `11/02/2026 14:30:05`: month first, to the whole second, with no time zone. Format it with [`DateTimeToString`](conversion.md#datetimetostring) before you show it or store it: [`DateTimeToString(DateGetUtc(), "yyyy-MM-dd")`](conversion.md#datetimetostring) gives today's date.

### DateGetYear

Returns the year of a date, such as 2026.

```c
int DateGetYear(date date)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `date` | `date` | The date. Text such as `2026-11-02` works too. |

**Returns** `int`: The year.
